title: Participant-Led Career Sprints and Access Workbook
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Overview:

This workbook formalizes a participant-driven approach to early career momentum at Redwood. It bundles: a repeatable sprint cadence for role-focused development, a prescriptive access and tooling checklist for new and transitioning contributors, and a short manager/mentor playbook to normalize expectations. The workbook is intended for new hires, people managers, mentors, and people-ops partners.

Why this exists:
- Reduce variability in the first 90 days for engineers, product, and platform contributors.
- Make access provisioning predictable and measurable (target: 48 business hours for full toolset).
- Align career sprint outcomes to competency ladders and role-level expectations.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: individual contributor onboarding (IC1–IC4), manager onboarding, cross-functional rotation support, and lateral role transitions. Does NOT replace role-specific technical onboarding labs for specialized infra or research tracks.
- Audience: new joiners, hiring managers, buddy/mentor, people-ops, engineering leads.

Definitions:
- Sprint: 14 calendar days focused on 1–2 measurable outcomes (e.g., merge a non-trivial PR, ship a docs-first integration).
- Access Bundle: standard set of accounts/entitlements required for a role to be productive (see Access Matrix).
- Activation Window: time between account creation request and completion. Target SLA: 48 business hours.

Owner and maintenance:
- Document owner: People Ops (Priya Nambiar)
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly review with engineering and product DRI (next review: 2026-05-15)
- Escalation path: people-ops -> hiring manager -> Head of People Ops.

Sprint design pattern (participant-led):
1) Kickoff (Day 0–1): participant selects a sprint goal with manager/mentor sign-off. Write a 1-paragraph success criteria.
2) Planning (Day 1–2): list tasks, blockers, and required accesses. Assign a buddy for technical review.
3) Execution (Day 3–12): daily check-ins (asynchronous ok) and two demo moments: mid-sprint and final demo.
4) Review (Day 13–14): public write-up of outcomes, artifacts (PRs, docs, tests), and a 1–3 line reflection.

Sprint examples (role-aligned):
- New Backend IC: ship a telemetry-enhanced endpoint behind feature flag + add an e2e smoke test.
- Product PM transition: run a 2-week scoped validation session with 5 customers and produce a prioritized decision memo.
- SRE rotation: run a pageload test for a non-critical service and update runbook with three remediation points.

Pre-sprint checklist (manager + people-ops):
1. Confirm role-level Access Bundle assigned.
2. Approve sprint goal and success criteria.
3. Assign buddy and reviewer.
4. Schedule mid-sprint demo slot.
5. Ensure workspace and required infra (test cluster, dataset mocks) available.

Access Matrix (standard bundles):
| Bundle name      | Typical roles           | Minimum entitlements (examples)                                        | Provision SLA |
|------------------|-------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| Core Contributor | IC1–IC3                 | Okta SSO, GSuite, GitHub (repo-read + team membership), Jira, Slack     | 48 business hrs |
| Engineer Plus    | IC2–IC4                 | + AWS console read, KMS request role, Redwood Console dev project view | 48 business hrs |
| Infra Operator   | SRE/Infra roles         | + Prod VPN, PagerDuty, Cluster admin (scoped)                         | 72 business hrs |
| Manager         | People/Eng Managers     | + Manager dashboards, 1:1 scheduling tools, compensation ladder view   | 48 business hrs |

Provisioning details and commands:
- Account requests: use the "Access Requests" form (URL internal: /tools/access-requests). Include new-joiner email, start date, team, and sprint intent.
- GitHub team invite: /cli (internal) -> `gh org invite --team \"team-name\" user@example.com`
- Okta SWAT ticket: create ticket in Jira project OPS-ACCESS with label `okta-provision`.
- Redwood Console project access: add to project via Console > Projects > Manage > Add Member (role: viewer/dev).

Service SLA & metrics to track:
- Activation Window: target median 24 hrs, p95 < 72 hrs.
- Sprint completion rate: percent of participant-led sprints that meet success criteria within 14 days (target 80%).
- Buddy review turnaround: median 48 hrs.

Role ladder alignment guidance (how sprints map to growth signals):
- IC1: deliver a scoped change with mentor support; demonstrate basic code quality and documentation.
- IC2: independently own an end-to-end small feature, instrumenting metrics and follow-up fixes.
- IC3: lead an integration across teams, propose design tradeoffs, mentor IC1/IC2 contributors.
- IC4+: shape priorities, own cross-product initiatives, and influence roadmap trade-offs.

Manager/mentor playbook (quick steps):
1. During offer stage: confirm Access Bundle and sprint expectation on offer email.
2. Day 0: set first sprint goal in the candidate's onboarding doc.
3. Day 1–2: unblock access requests and confirm buddy.
4. Mid-sprint: attend the demo and provide documented feedback (use template below).
5. Sprint review: update the individual's onboarding checklist and record signals for calibration conversation.

Manager feedback template (use in PR or demo notes):
- Sprint goal: (1–2 lines)
- Outcome: (success / partial / blocked)
- Evidence: (links to PRs, docs, dashboards)
- Coaching notes: (3 short bullets)
- Recommended next sprint focus: (1 sentence)

Artifacts to capture (required):
- Sprint README (1 page): goal, steps, blockers, artifacts, retrospective note.
- PRs and tests: linked to the sprint README.
- Buddy sign-off: one-line confirmation in the README.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: delayed access prevents execution. Mitigation: escalate to people-ops within 24 hrs; temporarily provide a sandbox environment.
- Failure: ambiguous sprint goal. Mitigation: require manager sign-off on success criteria before Day 2.
- Failure: no buddy engagement. Mitigation: people-ops maintains a rotating on-call buddy roster for core teams.

Onboarding tooling quick-reference (links and what to capture):
- HR / Payroll onboarding: capture W-4 / local tax forms, emergency contact, preferred name. Owner: People Ops.
- Okta: enable MFA, verify SSO groups. Owner: Security.
- GitHub: accept organization invite, set 2FA, join team repos. Owner: Eng Team Admin.
- Redwood Console sandbox: confirm project access and sample request to public models. Owner: Platform.

Templates (copy to new sprint page):
- Sprint README template: Title, Owner, Dates, Goal, Success criteria, Tasks, Blockers, Artifacts, Buddy sign-off, Retrospective notes.
- Demo slide template: 3 slides — Goal, Work completed (links), Learnings & next steps.

Privacy and confidentiality:
- Default confidentiality: internal. If a sprint involves customer PII or regulated data, mark the sprint page `restricted` and follow the Private Deployment onboarding checklist in the Security & Compliance space.

FAQ (short):
Q: What if a sprint is blocked by external dependencies?
A: Document the blocker, request dependency owner triage, and consider extending the sprint or pivoting to a different measurable task.

Q: Can managers assign sprint goals?
A: Yes — collaborative goal-setting is preferred. The participant should own the sprint and capture learnings.

Q: Where do I request expedited access?
A: Use the Access Requests form and select "expedite" with manager approval. People-ops will respond within business hours.

Appendix: sample sprint timeline (two-week example)
Day 0: Offer and first sprint proposal shared
Day 1: Access requests submitted
Day 2: Manager approves sprint and buddy assigned
Day 3–6: Development work + daily async updates
Day 7: Mid-sprint demo + feedback
Day 8–12: Finish tasks, open PRs, run tests
Day 13: Final demo, buddy sign-off
Day 14: Retrospective and next sprint planning

Contacts and ownership quick list:
- People Ops (onboarding & access): people-ops@redwood-inference.internal
- Platform access (Redwood Console): platform-admins@redwood-inference.internal
- Security (Okta/KMS): security@redwood-inference.internal
